literal: Misery-causing poverty will not exist for those who speak pleasure-giving sweet words towards anyone.
translation: Poverty, which brings misery, will never come to those who speak sweet words that bring joy to everyone.
modern: எல்லாரிடமும் இன்பம் தரும் இனிய சொற்களைப் பேசுபவர்களிடம், துன்பத்தைத் தரும் வறுமை அணுகாது.
explanation: This couplet links pleasant speech with the removal of life's hardships. The word 'துவ்வாமை' refers to poverty or destitution, which is described as 'துன்புறூஉம்' (that which causes misery). Conversely, 'இன்சொல்' (sweet words) are described as 'இன்புறூஉம்' (that which brings joy) to 'யார்மாட்டும்' (everyone). The poet asserts that those who consistently speak kindly to all will be spared from the suffering of poverty, as their pleasant nature naturally attracts goodwill, support, and prosperity.
